feedback on the status of claims  Maintain high levels of confidentiality whilst conducting investigations Identify gaps in workflow, process or policy whilst striving to provide upward feedback as required to further improve the experience for our customers Act as subject matter expert for change initiatives and/or cross functional projects taking place across the Aircover Scaled Ops and Optimization org, including assisting internal stakeholders to test, refine, ideate, and deploy new internal products and processes Your Expertise: 5+  years in a fintech or customer experience role , challenging customer problems and making claims decisions with consistency and fairness whilst adhering to policy terms and workflows Strong verbal and written communication skills with experience interacting with customers through multiple channels including email, messaging and phone  Active listening skills to understand user needs and provide personalized recommendations and assistance Ability to explain complex and sensitive issues to customers with confidence and clarity Analytical skills with the ability to organize and work independently with rapidly changing priorities experience Calm and Empathetic with ability to adapt to any situation by personalizing responses and educating our community whilst remaining level headed in challenging situations A regular work Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join:  The Chief Business Officer organization plays a pivotal role in driving the company’s growth and expansion efforts worldwide. Our teammates work on commercializing Airbnb’s new and existing businesses, helping Airbnb expand beyond its core offering as a place to stay. This includes recruiting and developing Airbnb’s global supply of high-quality stays, Experiences, and Services, and executing Airbnb’s global strategy in the market. With a focus on business strategy, quality supply and international expansion, the team is leading the way for Airbnb’s continued growth and success in its next chapter.  The Global Markets Team, which sits within CBO, ensures that Airbnb is locally relevant and serves the needs of our global hosts and guests, helping regions more efficiently plan and execute growth strategies across supply, demand, and other surfaces in a way that will resonate with our communities.  The Difference You Will Make :  You will work closely with the cross-functional leaders and teams, and play a key role in scaling our community growth and optimization-focused programs. The successful candidate will report to the Director, Programs and Business Operations.  A Typical Day:  Align all functions  to achieve Americas’s regional business objectives in partnership with the Director, Regional Business Operations and Growth. Own the conception, execution, and measurement of cross-functional initiatives end-to-end. Concretely, this means defining a crisp problem statement, articulating the ideal solution to that problem, identifying key dependencies blocking that solution, and then working with cross-functional stakeholders to achieve the solution. These initiatives will span across the demand, supply, and regulatory surfaces of the business.  Drive regular business operation meetings and initiate meaningful conversations - leading weekly meetings with cross-functional project teams (field & online operations, marketing, product, legal) to ensure key initiatives are on track. Use all available data sources and tools, internal and external, to analyze macro and micro trends, and present analysis, insights, and actionable plans to Airbnb country and regional leadership team to drive key business decisions.  Assist the Regional Director and Regional BizOps Director in owning the performance narrative for key metrics and deliver the story to senior leaders in a concise and clear manner in weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews Your Expertise:  Qualified candidates will ideally have a minimum of 10+ years of work experience, preferably with combined exposure to data-modeling, business analytics, and project management in a dynamic entrepreneurial environment.  A proven bias to action and ability to own a project from conception through to post-mortem. Ability to work in a world of uncertainty and ambiguity - to create clarity from chaos. A familiarity with AI, AI data analysis and AI tools would be considered an asset.  A world class written and verbal communicator with the ability to present at all levels of an organization in a succinct, clear and eloquent manner.  A proven track record of being able to storytell, influence and rally diverse cross-functional stakeholders against a common mission or goal using both qualitative and quantitative insights.  Ability to not only dive into details to drive execution but also zoom out to contextualize specific recommendations/initiatives within the broader company strategy.  Ability to multi-task by prioritizing work and coordinating required support across various functions to achieve project goals and objectives.  Impeccable organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to document processes & decisions made. Experience implementing and scaling initiatives across globally dispersed teams.  Experience working cross-functionally with multiple departments. Hands-on approach, getting things done fast.  Comfort with manipulating large datasets in excel is a must. SQL proficiency strongly preferred. Your Location: This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list  If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from. Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging: Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: reasonableaccommodations@airbnb.com . Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process.  We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application. How We'll Take Care of You: Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits.   Pay Range $168,000 — $203,000 USD   Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role. A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @ airbnb.com or @ ext.airbnb.com email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing.  We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. We encourage candidates to remain vigilant of these recruiting scams and not share sensitive information if you do not believe an individual is actually affiliated with Airbnb.

Job description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community you will join: The Chief Business Officer (CBO) organization drives Airbnb's growth and expansion around the world, commercializing our new and existing businesses and executing our global strategy in the market. The Global Markets team sits within CBO and makes sure Airbnb is locally relevant everywhere we operate, working with regions to plan and execute growth across supply, demand, and the surfaces our communities use. Asia is one of the largest growth opportunities in that portfolio and one of the most complex regions to run: Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia sit at very different stages of maturity, with distinct competitive sets, regulatory contexts and consumer behaviour. Over the past year, the region has built a new operating system and scaled multiple growth levers from single-market pilots to regional programs. That growth has outpaced our capacity to run it: business reporting, program delivery and the cross-functional roadmap currently sit with one person alongside the regional strategy agenda. We are building a dedicated capability to own how Asia operates and how Asia delivers, and we want you at the centre of it. The difference you will make: This role is based in Singapore and requires regular travel across Asia. In this role you report to the Senior Business Operations and Growth Lead, Asia and work closely with country Business Operations and Growth Leads across Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia, alongside central teams in growth marketing, product, payments, supply, policy and brand. You own the Asia business reporting and operating cadence, and you lead the delivery of the region's growth levers and its cross-functional roadmap. This is deliberately an ownership role in insights and execution, distinct from the roles around it. Countries own their market plans and outcomes, growth marketing, product and merchandising teams build the platforms, and Strategic Finance and Advanced Analytics own objective tracking and measurement standards. You own the connective tissue between them: the reporting that gives the region one accurate and current picture, the delivery of growth levers into market, the roadmap accountability that keeps cross-functional commitments on track, and the competitive read that tells us where we are gaining and losing. into the region's reporting, insight delivery and recurring operations that scales team output Synthesize data, trends, guest and host insights, and analysis into actionable recommendations for the regional business Conduct deep dives into operational, programs or functional topics as needed, working with FP&A to assess business performance across areas of strength and weakness Drive entity prioritization and lead entity setup across Asia markets, coordinating with legal, tax, finance and country teams Your expertise: 10+ years in business operations, strategy, consulting or program management, ideally in a marketplace, consumer technology, hospitality or online travel agency (OTA) environment Experience managing programs or operations across multiple countries with varying levels of maturity, and across time zones A proven track record building and running business operating cadences for a distributed organization: reporting, business reviews, and the follow-through that makes commitments land Exceptional cross-functional orchestration in a heavily matrixed organization, creating clarity where ownership is split across product, growth marketing, payments, supply and country teams Strong operating discipline: cross-workstream roadmaps, launch management, business reviews and executive reporting, and crisp written communication that keeps distributed teams aligned Builds operational leverage with AI: a track record of applying AI and automation to reporting, insight generation and repetitive operational work, with measurable time saved or scale gained. You treat this as part of how you work, not a side project. Analytical fluency: comfortable in the numbers, builds the analysis personally, and sets consistent measurement standards with analytics and finance partners (Excel) Thrives in ambiguity, with a strong bias to action, ownership and ruthless prioritization Fluent written and spoken English Desirable: hands-on experience with one or more growth levers such as incentives, promotions and coupons, host-funded offers, lifecycle and CRM, or merchandising. Job description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: Airbnb's Public Policy team works closely with federal, state and municipal governments, legislators, regulators, public entities, industry associations, academia, our host community and the broader public. We introduce them to Airbnb, highlight the social and economic contribution our community makes to Mexico and its local communities, and share best practices from around the world. Our goal is twofold. We want policymakers to understand the regulatory challenges that affect our hosts and to find models that work for cities, towns and their residents. We also want to help Mexican society embrace an innovative, collaborative economy where everyone can belong. As part of a wider regional policy team, we take part in many local, state and national conversations at once. We engage governments directly and involve our community and partners in making the case for fair, progressive home sharing rules. Our work is organized in local campaign pods that draw on a wide range of tools: detailed policy analysis, strategic partnerships, policy media, community organizing, digital tactics, polling, data science and research, and persuasive policy narratives. The Difference You will Make: The Public Policy Campaign Manager leads the design and execution of successful policy campaigns in Mexico, working with the Public Policy Lead on both daily operations and overall strategy. You will draft and run integrated engagement plans, using in-person and digital tools to move key stakeholders toward specific policy goals in response to active or developing legislation and regulation. A central part of the role is building trust with local authorities. You will help them understand the contribution our community makes, and engage them in creating fair legal and regulatory frameworks that embrace the potential of the sharing economy. You are meticulously organized, detail-oriented and focused on solutions. You see the big picture, prioritize strategically, and know which information and data to escalate to leadership. You turn big ideas into policy with a positive, creative outlook, and you build strong relationships with internal teams and stakeholders in Mexico, the region and globally. A Typical Day:  Develop and implement Airbnb's legislative and public policy activities in Mexico, including advocacy priorities, positions and strategies. Review legislative and regulatory language, draft comments and research issues to provide analysis on proposals affecting Airbnb's priorities. Build and represent Airbnb in coalitions and collaborations that advance our advocacy goals, creating them from scratch when needed. Maintain relationships with an extensive network of contacts in local, state and national legislative, executive and administrative offices, as well as allied groups and coalition partners. Represent Airbnb in meetings with government and elected officials, industry associations, Airbnb hosts and other stakeholders. Represent Airbnb at public speaking engagements as directed by the Public Policy Lead for Mexico & CCA. Recruit and manage consultants and agencies, and marshal external resources to execute campaign plans. Advise Airbnb teams on public policy matters to guide the development of products, services and policies. Work closely with local business partners so that campaign plans fit with business priorities and outcomes. Monitor and track legislation and regulatory matters, and advise the company on policy challenges. Report progress accurately and regularly, and flag roadblocks in a timely way. Your Expertise: At least 10 years of experience in public policy, direct lobbying or government relations in a business, political, governmental, legislative or regulatory context, such as tourism and accommodation, e-commerce and platform regulation, housing and landlord/tenant law, or tax. Proven experience managing complex regulatory and political issues, whether in-house, as a consultant, or in politics, campaigns or advocacy groups. Proficiency in regulatory and legislative drafting. Ability to quickly get up to speed on complex technical and regulatory issues. The Community You Will Join:  This position is employed by Airbnb Inc., however the role will provide direct support to Airbnb.org, an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit that focuses on emergency response and provides temporary housing for people in times of crisis. Airbnb.org is governed by an independent Board of Directors and its mission is to provide emergency housing in times of crisis. From Australia to France, hosts have offered to open up their homes and helped provide accommodations to over 250,000 people. Our goal is to exponentially increase Airbnb.org’s reach and impact over the next three years. Learn more at Airbnb.org .   The Difference You Will Make: You will manage Airbnb.org’s emergency responses in the APAC region but will also be expected to support responses globally as required. You will monitor disasters around the world, decide with your manager when an event meets our activation criteria, stand the response up, and manage it through to close-out. You will do this work with partners on the ground. Local nonprofits and agencies find displaced people, confirm eligibility, and provide case management. Your job is to make sure those partners are ready before an event, and that during one they have the housing supply, the guidance, and the answers they need. Speed matters, and so does the quality of the placement. You will run several responses at the same time, in different countries and at different stages. You will keep internal teams and external partners informed before they have to ask. You will work across Operations, Strategic Partnerships, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Finance, and Product to deliver one coordinated response. Reporting to the Senior Lead of Global Emergency Response, this position requires a background in humanitarian and disaster response operations, strong leadership, and expertise in building effective partnerships with nonprofits and government agencies. Experience in Social Impact for tech companies is a big plus. Much of the work is not defined in advance. You will need to set direction yourself, decide with incomplete information, and move things toward clarity and action. You must also be able to deploy to the field on short notice to manage disaster response programs on the ground if needed.    A Typical Day:  Monitor global disasters via news, partner alerts, government advisories, and internal signals to assess and recommend responses based on Airbnb.org criteria. Establish, activate, and oversee emergency housing responses in close collaboration with on-the-ground partners responsible for the intake and case management of individuals displaced by disasters. Oversee diverse, simultaneous disaster responses. Set priorities across them, and hold an accurate record of status, spend, and the number of people housed. Proactively communicate status, decisions, and next steps to internal and external cross-functional stakeholders and partners. Manage each response end-to-end: verify partner readiness, determine response size and stay lengths, launch operations, monitor placements, solve issues, and conclude based on clear exit criteria. Manage partnerships (including onboarding new partners and managing existing partners) during active emergencies, and ensuring smooth handoff to the Partnerships team at the conclusion of emergency responses. Promptly answer partner questions during live responses, escalating unresolved ones. Work closely with the Partnerships team to build and manage partnerships with organizations that vet and support guests, while working with our Operations team to optimize housing supply, reduce costs, and maximize positive impact for those affected. Sharpen activation criteria and playbooks, pre-position partner agreements, expand 24/7 global coverage, increase team capacity, and advocate for the product features the operation needs. Integrate best practices from experts and agencies, and cultivate relationships with government bodies and emergency management authorities in key regions before an event happens. Deploy to disaster zones on short notice to manage ground operations, and hand over cleanly when you leave. Write the after-action review for each response, and make sure the changes it calls for actually happen. Clear, timely, and proactive communication with internal and external cross-functional stakeholders and partners, in writing and in person. A proactive self-starter. Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence across functions and teams you do not manage. Il s'agit d'un rôle de leadership opérationnel qui exige une expérience considérable en service à la clientèle et en gestion d'équipe. De solides compétences organisationnelles et la capacité de concilier le travail en temps réel et le travail planifié sont également requises. Ils doivent également être adaptables et réactifs dans notre environnement au rythme rapide, parfois sous pression, tout en demeurant flexibles, proactifs, ingénieux, efficaces et en démontrant un haut niveau de professionnalisme et de confidentialité. Job description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. La communauté à laquelle vous vous joindrez Vous deviendrez un membre clé de l’équipe de planification du soutien à la communauté des Opérations mondiales. Cette équipe pilote le processus de planification de la feuille de route, de bout en bout, pour le soutien à la communauté d’Airbnb. Elle veille à ce que les initiatives et les programmes soient priorisés en fonction de notre stratégie globale et de notre engagement à offrir une expérience client exceptionnelle. Nous sommes une équipe mondiale experte en planification stratégique, en gestion des parties prenantes, en collaboration interfonctionnelle et en efficacité organisationnelle. La différence que vous ferez À titre de partenaire principal de planification, Contenu, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel dans la réussite et la satisfaction de notre clientèle grâce à une gestion des relations rigoureuse et à une collaboration stratégique. Vous soutiendrez un ou plusieurs domaines de produits et serez la personne-ressource principale des gestionnaires de contenu, des rédacteurs et rédactrices ainsi que des stratèges de ces domaines. Vous assurerez la planification et la coordination de bout en bout de chaque lancement qui a une incidence sur le contenu du soutien à la communauté. Vous veillerez à ce que la communication soit claire, que les objectifs soient harmonisés et que le contenu soit livré à temps et avec un haut niveau de qualité au moment du lancement. Vous repérerez de façon proactive les occasions d’ajouter de la valeur tout en vous attaquant aux difficultés potentielles, avec toujours en tête d’obtenir des résultats mesurables pour notre clientèle et pour l’entreprise. Votre capacité à établir des relations de confiance avec les partenaires du contenu, du produit, de l’ingénierie, du marketing et des affaires juridiques, alliée à votre esprit stratégique et à votre rigueur d’exécution, contribuera au bon déroulement des lancements ainsi qu’à la réussite de notre clientèle et de l’organisation. Une journée type Établir un dialogue proactif avec les partenaires et les parties prenantes interfonctionnels : suivis réguliers, communication des échéanciers de planification et des jalons à venir, séances de rétroaction. Le but est de bâtir la confiance et de s’assurer de l’harmonisation avec leurs buts et objectifs. Déterminer à l’avance toutes les personnes responsables de chaque lancement : le rédacteur ou la rédactrice et le ou la stratège du contenu touché; les personnes chargées d’approuver le contenu pour le marketing, les affaires juridiques et l’expertise technique; les partenaires de localisation; et les partenaires interfonctionnels, comme la taxonomie, la formation, le centre de ressources, Biztech et les autres gestionnaires de projet dont les travaux sont liés. Élaborer le calendrier du contenu et le communiquer à toutes les personnes qui demandent du contenu et à celles qui l’approuvent. Pour ce faire, recueillir les dates d’indisponibilité des personnes chargées d’approuver et prévoir du temps pour les audits de contenu, la rédaction, la vérification de l’exactitude technique, la révision par le marketing, la révision juridique et la localisation, ainsi qu’une marge pour les imprévus. Planifier et animer la série de réunions de chaque lancement : la séance de collecte d’information sur le lancement avec les équipes du produit, de l’ingénierie et de la préparation au lancement; les séances d’audit de contenu; une réunion préalable au lancement avec le marketing; une réunion hebdomadaire récurrente sur l’état du lancement avec l’équipe de contenu et les experts techniques; et, le jour du lancement, une réunion « Mission Control » et un canal Slack. Collaborer avec les stratèges lors des audits de contenu pour repérer tout le contenu touché, en hiérarchiser les répercussions (P1 : jour du lancement; P2 : suivis à court terme; P3 : tous les autres éléments), s’assurer qu’un billet est ouvert pour chaque article touché et signaler le contenu lié à l’interface utilisateur ainsi que les exigences de localisation. Préparer et envoyer chaque semaine un compte rendu de l’état d’avancement aux gestionnaires de contenu et aux personnes responsables du contenu, incluant la liste des articles touchés et leur état P1/P2/P3, afin que les risques (calendrier des audits, approbations en retard, changements de date de lancement) soient visibles rapidement. Anticiper les risques et les problèmes, et élaborer de façon proactive des stratégies d’atténuation (aller au-delà du simple suivi de l’état d’avancement et mener les problèmes jusqu’à leur résolution). Maintenir un processus pour repérer les demandes de contenu tardives et les signaler comme étant « à risque ». Envoyer régulièrement des rappels aux personnes ayant des responsabilités liées au lancement et, lorsque les personnes chargées d’approuver ne répondent pas en mode asynchrone, planifier des rencontres d’approbation en direct avec le marketing, l’ingénierie, les affaires juridiques et d’autres intervenants. Préparer des communications interfonctionnelles à l’intention des équipes partenaires touchées par notre travail, comme la localisation, Biztech, la gestion des connaissances et la formation. Coordonner en temps réel la mise en ligne le jour du lancement, une fois le feu vert donné par l’équipe de préparation au lancement, afin que l’équipe de contenu sache qu’elle peut publier en toute sécurité. Participer aux réunions de lancement, aux séances de coordination en temps réel et aux séances du centre de contact organisées par d’autres équipes afin d’être la voix de l’équipe de contenu, de faire le point, de répondre aux questions et de tenir l’équipe de contenu informée des problèmes émergents. Épargner aux rédacteurs et rédactrices les questions logistiques, obtenir les renseignements et les approbations manquants et lever les obstacles, afin de leur permettre de se consacrer au contenu. Préparer à l’intention de la direction une bilan de lancement qui décrit ce qui a été publié et le rendement du contenu, et tenir un registre du contenu publié pour alimenter les rapports, mettre en valeur les réussites et documenter les leçons apprises. Suivre l’état des dossiers transmis à un palier supérieur après le lancement et en rendre compte. Favoriser l’amélioration continue et la simplification des processus de planification du contenu, et mettre en place des mécanismes de rétroaction qui permettent de communiquer les suites données aux partenaires et aux parties prenantes. Votre expertise Au moins 8 ans d’expérience dans des postes de planification stratégique, de gestion de programmes ou d’opérations d’affaires, avec des réussites démontrées. Expérience avérée du pilotage de processus de planification interfonctionnelle ou de gestion de portefeuille, avec une exposition à la haute direction. Compétences exceptionnelles en communication (orale, écrite et présentations) auprès de tous les niveaux d’une organisation. Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et en analyse, ainsi qu’une bonne compréhension de la mise en œuvre de systèmes et de la gestion du changement. Maîtrise des outils de collaboration à distance et de gestion de projet, comme Asana, Jira et Airtable. Esprit stratégique et sens de l’organisation, et capacité de travailler en collaboration avec différentes équipes. Connaissance pratique du cycle de vie et des méthodologies de développement de produits logiciels. Une expérience concrète de la méthodologie Agile est un atout. Capacité éprouvée à désamorcer les situations tendues et à résoudre les conflits de façon professionnelle et empathique. Capacité de gérer simultanément plusieurs lancements et priorités concurrentes, tout en veillant à ce que les livrables soient remis à temps et dans le respect de la portée du projet. Aisance à composer avec des priorités changeantes et capacité de proposer des solutions dans un environnement dynamique, ambigu et au rythme soutenu. Expérience de la planification ou de la coordination de lancements de contenu, de gestion des connaissances ou de produits. Votre emplacement : En raison de la nature de ce poste, le candidat retenu devra être basé au Canada pour pouvoir effectuer son travail. Actuellement, les employés peuvent être situés dans : la Colombie-Britannique, l'Ontario, le Québec, l'Alberta ou le Saskatchewan. Cette liste est continuellement mise à jour, veuillez vérifier avec nous si les provinces dans lesquelles vous vivez figurent sur la liste. Si votre poste est employé par une autre entité Airbnb, votre recruteur vous informera des provinces dans lesquelles vous êtes éligible pour travailler. Notre engagement envers l’inclusion et l’appartenance : Airbnb s'engage à travailler avec le vivier de talents le plus large possible. Nous pensons que la diversité des idées favorise l’innovation et l’engagement, et nous permet d’attirer des personnes créatives et de développer les meilleurs produits, services et solutions. Toutes les personnes qualifiées sont encouragées à postuler. Nous nous efforçons également de proposer un processus de candidature et d'entretien inclusif pour les personnes handicapées. Si vous êtes un candidat handicapé et avez besoin d'aménagements raisonnables pour soumettre une candidature, veuillez nous contacter à l'adresse : raisonnableaccommodations@airbnb.com. Veuillez inclure votre nom complet, le poste pour lequel vous postulez et les aménagements nécessaires pour vous aider dans le processus de recrutement.  Nous vous demandons de nous contacter uniquement si vous êtes un candidat dont le handicap vous empêche de remplir notre candidature en ligne. Nous utilisons des outils automatisés pour aider notre équipe de recrutement à examiner efficacement un grand nombre de candidatures. Toutes les décisions finales d’embauche sont prises par une personne humaine. Ce poste correspond à un poste vacant au sein de l'organisation. How We'll Take Care of You: Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range shown below is annualized, is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits. Canada Annual Pay Range $102,000 — $128,000 CAD   Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role. A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @ airbnb.com or @ ext.airbnb.com email addresses. These partnerships unlock access to millions of listings and directly shape the quality and reliability of the host and guest experience. At the center of this work are our Connectivity Partner Managers, who own Airbnb's relationships with these third-party technology providers — PMS (Property Management System), channel manager, and revenue management tool vendors that hosts and property managers use to sync listings, calendars, pricing, and reservations with Airbnb. Connectivity Partner Managers are the primary point of contact for these partners: they ensure integrations meet Airbnb's connectivity standards, resolve sync and data issues, onboard new partners, negotiate partnership terms, drive adoption of Airbnb's APIs among software vendors, and work with Product and Engineering to prioritize roadmap improvements based on partner feedback. The Difference You Will Make We're looking for a seasoned Senior Enablement Manager to build and own end-to-end enablement for Airbnb's API team and Connectivity Partner Managers across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. This is a newly approved, full-time role created to close a resourcing gap: enablement support for API has historically been covered informally and part-time, and this role will stand up a sustainable, scalable enablement function from the ground up. The core of this role is to enable our Connectivity Partner Managers to do their jobs more effectively and drive tangible impact. Connectivity Partner Managers own the full relationship with PMS, channel manager, and revenue management tool partners — from onboarding and integration standards to sync/data issue resolution, contract negotiation, API adoption, and roadmap prioritization with Product and Engineering. You will build the onboarding curriculum, training, playbooks, and certifications that ramp new Connectivity Partner Managers; keep them current on product launches, API versions, and roadmap changes; and equip them with the narratives, tools, and processes they need to manage partner relationships and escalations with confidence. This is a highly cross-functional, more technical role than a typical field-enablement position — it requires deep, ongoing engagement with the Product roadmap and with Connectivity Partner Managers themselves, not a copy-paste of a direct-sales enablement playbook. You will own onboarding, training, and continuous development for teams supporting API partners; drive consistent acquisition, growth, and retention of high-quality supply; and localize global enablement programs for regional relevance. Job description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: Everyone at Airbnb thinks about trust, but our team obsesses over it daily. At the core of trust is safety, and thus we spend a significant amount of our time and energy keeping the community safe. The Trust team is responsible for developing the technology that helps protect our community and platform from fraud while also ensuring our hosts, guests, homes, and experiences meet our high standards. We constantly work to fight against online fraud (such as monetary loss, compromised accounts, spam and scam in messages, fake inventory, etc.) as well as offline fraud (theft, property damage, personal safety, etc.). We also work on onboarding and screening of users, and think about complex topics like identity and reputation to ensure that every interaction with Airbnb helps build trust in us and our community. The Trust Frontier AI team is where new AI technology for Trust gets invented and proven. We build specialized models for mission-critical trust and safety problems, develop the AI agents and agentic capabilities that automate trust decisions, and create the benchmarks and evaluation harnesses that keep decision quality high as those agents take on more autonomy. Develop specialized models for trust and safety use cases, and use LLMs and AI agents to accelerate how we build models. Write, review, and ship clean, testable code — whether training a new model, improving an existing pipeline, or optimizing a feature for scalability and reliability. Experience with data engineering and building end-to-end ML pipelines, including both batch and real-time systems. Experience designing evaluation methodology for ML or LLM systems — benchmarks, ground truth, offline/online metrics, calibration. Partner with platform and product teams to influence the AI tooling roadmap based on the needs of non-technical users. Direct external partner and consulting engagements, including scope, governance, and return on investment. Role model Airbnb's core values and strengthen the company's mission through the way AI is introduced to employees. You'll work across orgs to identify the themes that connect work from multiple teams, and publish them as connected sets — while each domain keeps publishing in depth for its own specialists. Build our voices. Help our engineers and technical leaders develop genuine public presence: bylines, talks, speaker coaching, and a pipeline of new voices. This includes partnering closely with our CTO to establish his public technical presence. Own distribution. Establish our canonical home on an Airbnb-owned domain, stand up the surfaces we're missing including video, and decide what our social channels are for. Publishing well and distributing poorly is the pattern we're here to break. Run our external presence. Set conference and event strategy — where we speak, where we sponsor, where we skip — and manage what we host ourselves. Own our academic collaborations and technical media relationships, and the budget and vendors behind all of it. Steward our open source presence. Make sure what Airbnb claims publicly is accurate and actually maintained, and that the projects carrying our name reflect how we want to be seen. Prove it works. You've owned events, budgets and vendors end to end, and you're comfortable with the unglamorous half of the job. Measurement literacy. You connect brand work to funnel outcomes, and you're straight about the limits of attribution rather than reaching for impressions. Judgment on risk. You've navigated legal and security review, and you know what shouldn't be published as well as what should. Experience helping a senior executive build a public technical presence. Familiarity with AI and ML engineering topics, and with academic or research communications. Job description:
About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month. You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI. Key responsibilities Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline. Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments. Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge. Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership. Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting. Serve as the primary contact for external auditors. Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready. Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer. Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close. Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close. Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements. Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326). Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments. Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries. Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence. Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes. Minimum qualifications Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue. Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis. Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger. Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes. Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations. Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits. Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams. Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built. Preferred qualifications Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams. A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA). Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company. Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace). Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models. Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools. Experience with IPO readiness. Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.  For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $190,000 — $230,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage:  Learn about  our policy for using AI in our application process.

Job description:
About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. Anthropic Fellows Program overview The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience. Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis. Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you. What to expect 4 months of full-time research  Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers  Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country) Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses Interview process The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Compensation The expected base stipend for this role is 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension). The Anthropic Institute Fellows (Economics & Policy) Mentors, research areas, & past projects Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential research areas and mentors include: Economics Maxim Massenkoff Peter McCrory Policy, Security, and Society Jack Clark Marina Favaro Jim Baker Projects in this workstream may include: Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society Analysing the offense–defense balance for AI-enabled cyber and bio capabilities as models scale Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement For past project examples, see: How AI Impacts Skill Formation : Judy Shen and Alex Tamkin Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models : Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman, and Esin Durmus Unique candidate criteria You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you: Have an interest in economics or policy research; prior experience in this area is a plus but not required Are adaptable and collaborative, able to take direction and contribute to team priorities rather than needing to pursue a predetermined research agenda Are skilled at writing up and communicating your results, even when they're null or unexpected Are passionate about translating research insights into actionable recommendations for improving AI systems and informing policy You may be a good fit if you: Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole Are excited to transition into AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic Strong track record of empirical research Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly Candidates must be: Fluent in Python programming Available to work full-time on the Fellows program Logistics - Fellows Program Submit your application to the Anthropic Institute Fellows at the bottom of this page. Logistics Requirements:  To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program. Workspace Locations: We have designated shared workspaces in SF.  We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada .  Visa Sponsorship: We are not currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada. Program Duration: The program runs for 4 months, full-time. If you can't commit to the full duration, please still apply and note your constraints in the application. We review these requests on a case-by-case basis.     The below are Anthropic's policies for full time roles. These do NOT apply to the Fellows Program. Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage:  Learn about  our policy for using AI in our application process.

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. À propos d’Anthropic La mission d’Anthropic est de créer des systèmes d’IA fiables, interprétables et orientables. Nous voulons que l'IA soit sûre et bénéfique pour nos utilisateurs et pour la société dans son ensemble. Notre équipe est composée de chercheurs, d'ingénieurs, d'experts politiques et de chefs d'entreprise engagés qui travaillent ensemble pour créer des systèmes d'IA bénéfiques. À propos du poste En tant qu'architecte des solutions partenaires au sein de l'équipe d'IA appliquée d'Anthropic, vous serez architecte avant-vente chargé d'entretenir des relations techniques avec nos intégrateurs de systèmes mondiaux et régionaux (GSI/RSI) et nos partenaires cloud (AWS et GCP). Vous renforcerez nos relations avec les partenaires clés pour accélérer les revenus indirects, permettre leurs pratiques d'IA et exécuter la stratégie GTM à long terme. Responsabilités: Partenariat technique stratégique  : soyez un partenaire de réflexion technique pour l'équipe des partenariats Anthropic GTM, en apportant une expertise technique pour mieux comprendre l'environnement des partenaires, en pilotant des programmes stratégiques clés et en identifiant des opportunités pour approfondir leurs compétences techniques. Vous vous intégrez aux équipes techniques de GSI et des partenaires cloud pour mettre en œuvre leurs pratiques en matière d'IA, vous aider à résoudre les problèmes, promouvoir Anthropic au sein de leurs communautés de développeurs et servir de point d'accès pour les problèmes techniques complexes. Développement conjoint de solutions : Collaborer avec des partenaires pour identifier des applications GenAI spécifiques à grande valeur industrielle, développer des solutions conjointes et codifier des architectures de référence / bonnes pratiques afin d’accélérer le temps de déploiement Assistance aux offres clients : Intervenir directement pour débloquer des transactions clients stratégiques où les partenaires sont le principal vecteur de livraison, apportant une expertise technique approfondie et des conseils en architecture de solutions. Écosystème de partenaires et événements : représentez Anthropic lors d'événements partenaires tels que les ateliers clients GSI, les sommets AWS et les conférences sectorielles. Animer ou soutenir des événements, hackathons et sessions de formation technique destinés aux développeurs partenaires, en particulier pour les communautés ayant une expertise technique pointue. Retours sur les produits : validez et recueillez des retours sur les produits et services d'Anthropic, notamment en ce qui concerne les cas d'utilisation et modèles de déploiement des partenaires, et transmettez ces commentaires aux équipes Anthropic concernées afin d'éclairer la feuille de route du produit et la stratégie des partenaires. Profil recherché: Plus de 5 ans d'expérience dans des rôles techniques orientés clients et partenaires, tels que Architecte de Solutions, Ingénieur Commercial, Ingénieur Commercial Partenaires, Responsable de Compte Technique Expérience avérée de partenariats fructueux avec des intégrateurs de systèmes mondiaux et/ou des fournisseurs de services cloud pour résoudre des problèmes techniques complexes, de la conception initiale de la solution à sa mise en œuvre chez le client Capacité exceptionnelle à établir des relations avec diverses parties prenantes et à leur communiquer des concepts techniques, notamment des cadres supérieurs, des équipes informatiques et d'ingénierie, etc. Solides compétences en présentation et communication technique avec la capacité de traduire les exigences entre parties prenantes techniques et commerciales Expérience de la conception d'architectures cloud évolutives et de l'intégration avec des systèmes d'entreprise Familiarité avec les cadres et outils LLM courants ou une formation en apprentissage automatique ou en science des données Enthousiasme à l'idée de participer à une collaboration inter-organisationnelle, de trouver des compromis et de trouver un équilibre entre des priorités concurrentes L'amour de l'enseignement, du mentorat et de la réussite des autres Passion pour la réflexion créative sur la manière d'utiliser la technologie de façon sûre et bénéfique, et qui favorise ultimement l'avancement des systèmes d'IA sûrs. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As an Applied AI Architect on the Partnerships team at Anthropic, you will be a pre-sales architect focused on cultivating technical relationships with our Global and Regional System Integrators (GSIs/RSIs), and our cloud partners (AWS and GCP). You will strengthen our relationships with key partners to accelerate indirect revenue, enable their AI practices, and execute on long-term GTM strategy. Responsibilities: Strategic Technical Partnership : Be a technical thought partner to the Anthropic GTM partnerships team, providing technical expertise to better understand the partner landscape, driving key strategic programs, and identifying opportunities to deepen partner technical capabilities. Embed with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, support troubleshooting, evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities, and serve as an escalation point for complex technical issues. Joint Solution Development: Collaborate with partners to identify high value industry-specific GenAI applications, develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures / best practices to accelerate time to deployment Customer Deal Support:  Intervene directly to unblock strategic customer deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep technical expertise and solution architecture guidance. Partner Ecosystem & Events: Represent Anthropic at partner events such as GSI customer workshops, AWS summits, and industry conferences. Lead or support partner-specific developer events, hackathons, and technical enablement sessions, especially for technically native communities.Product Feedback: Validate and gather feedback on Anthropic's products and offerings, especially as they relate to partner use cases and deployment patterns, and deliver this feedback to relevant Anthropic teams to inform product roadmap and partner strategy. You may be a good fit if you have: 5+ years of experience in technical customer-facing/partner-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner Sales Engineer, Technical Account Manager Track record of successfully partnering with GSIs and/or cloud providers to solve complex technical challenges, from initial solution design through customer delivery Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more Strong presentation & technical communication skills with the ability to translate requirements between technical and business stakeholders Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.  For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: €190.000 — €220.000 EUR Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Job description:
About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role: As a Partners Solutions Architect on the Applied AI team at Anthropic, you will be a Pre-Sales architect focused on cultivating technical relationships with our Global and Regional System Integrators (GSIs/RSIs), and our cloud partners (AWS, GCP, and Azure). You will strengthen our relationships with key partners to accelerate indirect revenue, enable their AI practices, and execute on long-term GTM strategy. Responsibilities: Strategic Technical Partnership : Be a technical thought partner to the Anthropic GTM partnerships team, providing technical expertise to better understand the partner landscape, driving key strategic programs, and identifying opportunities to deepen partner technical capabilities. Embed with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, support troubleshooting, evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities, and serve as an escalation point for complex technical issues. Joint Solution Development: Collaborate with partners to identify high value industry-specific GenAI applications, develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures / best practices to accelerate time to deployment Customer Deal Support:  Intervene directly to unblock strategic customer deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep technical expertise and solution architecture guidance. Partner Ecosystem & Events: Represent Anthropic at partner events such as GSI customer workshops, AWS summits, and industry conferences. Lead or support partner-specific developer events, hackathons, and technical enablement sessions, especially for technically native communities.Product Feedback: Validate and gather feedback on Anthropic's products and offerings, especially as they relate to partner use cases and deployment patterns, and deliver this feedback to relevant Anthropic teams to inform product roadmap and partner strategy. You may be a good fit if you have: 5+ years of experience in technical customer-facing/partner-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner Sales Engineer, Technical Account Manager Track record of successfully partnering with GSIs and/or cloud providers to solve complex technical challenges, from initial solution design through customer delivery Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more Strong presentation & technical communication skills with the ability to translate requirements between technical and business stakeholders Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.  For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $275,000 — $380,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage:  Learn about  our policy for using AI in our application process.

Much of this work is drug repurposing: testing new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.
